incidents.body:
Resolved — This issue is resolved. Between August 18 at 1:03 PM ET and August 20 at 11:49 AM ET, files attached to Government Cloud form submissions were not saved due to a storage configuration issue introduced during a hosting architecture change. Form submissions completed and responses were saved; only the uploaded files were affected.

Files uploaded during this window were not stored and cannot be recovered. They will need to be submitted again. All other response data is intact.

Uploads have been working normally since August 20 at 11:49 AM ET, and we have verified successful uploads across multiple accounts. Customers with questions about specific responses should contact FormAssembly Support.
incidents.title: Gov Cloud accounts: File Uploads breaking responses

incidents.body:
You may be aware of a widespread AWS outage this morning. This event impacted FormAssembly, and we want to provide details on what happened and our current status.

What Happened: Amazon Web Services (AWS) experienced a significant DNS resolution failure in their US-EAST-1 region starting around 12:11 AM ET. This had a cascading impact on many AWS services globally, as many rely on this core region.

How This Affected FormAssembly :Our primary infrastructure runs in AWS US-EAST-1. As a result, we experienced degraded performance and service disruptions. The impact was felt across many services we use.

Current Status: AWS mitigated the primary DNS issue by 3:35 AM ET, and most core services have recovered after working through significant backlogs.
While the major disruption is over, we are still observing some sporadic performance issues. You may still experience some lingering, intermittent slowness as these services fully stabilize.

Next Steps: Our team is continuing to actively monitor the situation until all services report stable, normal performance.
incidents.title: AWS US-EAST-1 Outage - Monitoring Recovery
